Recursion is a technique where a function solves a problem by calling itself with a smaller piece of that same problem. Every recursive function needs a **base case** — a simple condition that stops the recursion — otherwise it will call itself forever and crash. Each time the function calls itself, the problem gets smaller, until it finally reaches the base case, and then the answers "unwind" back up the call stack to give you the final result. A classic example is factorial: `factorial(n) = n × factorial(n-1)`, with the base case `factorial(1) = 1`.
